minutes.headline: ZBA denied the special permit for a rottweiler kennel at 110 Fire Road 12, then upheld the building commissioner on a fence.
minutes.summary: The board heard a special permit application for a dog kennel on Lake Shirley, with many letters and speakers opposed and the police chief saying no license would be issued. A motion to deny the permit was made and the petition was denied. A continued hearing followed on an appeal over a six-foot fence on Sunset Lane; the motion that the building commissioner erred failed and his decision was upheld.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals denied the special permit for a dog kennel at 110 Fire Road 12 after a long hearing with many opposed speakers.
The kennel decision is to be filed with the town clerk within 14 days, and an appeal to superior court can be made within 20 days.
On the continued hearing, the motion that the building inspector erred on the Sunset Lane fence failed, with two in favor and four needed.
The building commissioner's decision on the fence at 30 Sunset Lane was upheld because the motion did not reach four votes.
The police chief told the board that no kennel license would be issued, and speakers raised noise and lake water quality.

why_it_matters: The denial means no kennel can operate at the Lake Shirley address under this petition, which bears on noise and lake water quality for neighbors.
The fence ruling shows that an appeal against a building commissioner needs four votes to succeed, so a split board leaves the original decision in place.
watch_next: The written kennel decision to be filed with the town clerk within 14 days, then a 20-day window to appeal to superior court.
